notes:
West Bengal (18th Assembly, elected 23-29 Apr 2026 + Falta repoll 21 May 2026, results 4/24 May 2026): 294 seats -> 292 filled + 2 vacant (Nandigram & Rejinagar, both vacated by winners who contested two seats: Suvendu Adhikari and Humayun Kabir). The AITC legislature party split after its defeat into Democratic Trinamool Congress (DTC, 65, led by Ritabrata Banerjee, Leader of Opposition) and Mamata All India Trinamool Congress (MAITC, 15, led by Mamata Banerjee) -- this is reflected in the st-wb-assembly entity stats (sourced to the assembly's own infobox, dated 25 Sep 2026) but NOT fully reconciled at the individual position level: Wikipedia's member-by-member table still tags 56 of these MLAs plain 'AITC' (vs 24 explicitly 'DTC') because its per-row updates lag the aggregate count; those 56 positions are recorded with party 'AITC' and confidence 'low', flagged for a follow-up pass once individual DTC/MAITC membership can be confirmed (e.g. via West Bengal Legislative Assembly Secretariat seating list or further press coverage). Holder names use the election-results/individual-article spelling where the current-assembly table's spelling differed (both refer to the same person in every checked case except Raina (SC), where 'Souvik Patra' in the current-assembly table appears to be a typo for 'Subhash Patra', confirmed via his own Wikipedia article and the election-results table).

Assam (16th Assembly, elected 9 Apr 2026): all 126 seats filled, unchanged from the election result; no by-elections/deaths/defections found. Note: the pre-existing st-as-assembly.stats in data/raw/states-wb-as-sk.json had 'MAITC: 1' -- corrected here to 'AITC: 1' since MAITC did not exist until West Bengal's post-May-2026 TMC split (Assam's TMC winner, Chandan Brahma in Kokrajhar, predates that split).

Sikkim (11th Assembly, elected 19 Apr 2024): all 32 seats SKM. Two June 2024 resignations (CM Prem Singh Tamang vacated Soreng-Chakung, retaining Rhenock; his wife Krishna Kumari Rai resigned Namchi-Singhithang a day after being sworn in) were refilled unopposed in October 2024 by-elections by Aditya Tamang and Satish Chandra Rai respectively -- both recorded as current holders with since=2024-10-29. No vacancies.

Reservation tags: WB (SC)/(ST) taken from the 2026 election-results table (64 SC + 15 ST); Sikkim uses its own (BL)=Bhutia-Lepcha [12 seats], (SC) [2 seats], (BM)=Sangha/Buddhist-Monasteries [1 seat] categories rather than the generic SC/ST scheme, preserved as Wikipedia labels them since that is more accurate than forcing them into SC/ST. Assam constituency list had no reservation-tag mismatches to flag.

verification.method: 1) Structural/ID/schema validation via python (uniqueness, per-house counts, st-<code>-pos- ID pattern). 2) Confirmed current (latest) house used for each state: WB 18th Assembly (Apr-May 2026, term began 15 May 2026, supersedes 17th), AS 16th Assembly (Apr 2026), SK 11th Assembly (Apr 2024, mid-term, no newer election) -- all correct. 3) Re-fetched live Wikipedia wikitext (18th_West_Bengal_Assembly, 16th_Assam_Assembly, Sikkim_Legislative_Assembly + 2024_Sikkim_Legislative_Assembly_election) via the MediaWiki API and wrote a custom rowspan-aware table parser (independent of the original agent's) to reconstruct the full current member roster per state, then diffed it seat-by-seat against this file: WB 282/294 seats auto-matched cleanly (12 missed by parser-side constituency-name regex gaps, not file errors), AS 122/126 auto-matched (4 missed similarly), SK cross-checked at full-roster level via the election/assembly articles. 4) Searched WB and AS wikitext for by-election/resignation/death/disqualification/vacancy mentions since the current term began (2025-2026 window); found none beyond what the file already records (WB: Nandigram & Rejinagar still vacant, no by-election held yet; AS: none; SK: the Jun-Oct 2024 resignation/by-election pair, already in file, predates the 2025-2026 window and no further changes found). 5) Attempted independent non-Wikipedia spot checks (ECI, wbassembly/assamassembly/sikkimassembly official sites); the state-assembly domains did not resolve from this sandbox's network and eci.gov.in did not expose an easily machine-parseable constituency-level results page in the time available, so this leg fell back to the file's existing two-Wikipedia-source citations (election-results article + current-assembly article), which the auto-diff in step 3 already exercises across nearly the full roster (well beyond a 30-member sample).
verification.findingsSummary: No data errors found. 4 candidate party mismatches surfaced by the independent re-parse (WB: Dum Dum/Rajarhat New Town/Bidhannagar/Rajarhat Gopalpur; AS: Jaleshwar) were all traced to a rowspan-carry bug in this verifier's own parser (a same-row 'No.' cell also carrying a rowspan attribute caused the party template on that row to be skipped), not to errors in the file -- the file's BJP/INC values for those seats are correct per the raw wikitext. 25 (WB) + 6 (AS) holder-name spelling/transliteration variants exist between Wikipedia's current-assembly table and its individual biography articles (e.g. 'Ashis' vs 'Ashim', 'Md.' vs 'Mohammad'); the file already and correctly prefers individual-article spelling per its own documented policy (see the Raina/Subhash Patra note already in the file), so none of these were changed. The st-wb-assembly entity 'stats' patch (BJP 207, DTC 65, MAITC 15, INC 2, AJUP 1, CPI(M) 1, ISF 1, Vacant 2) was independently re-verified against the assembly's own live infobox aggregate on its Wikipedia page and matches exactly -- left unchanged. Summing individual position holder.party values instead gives BJP 207 / AITC 56 / DTC 24 / INC 2 / AJUP 1 / CPI(M) 1 / ISF 1 / Vacant 2 (same total, different AITC/DTC/MAITC split): this is a genuine, already-documented lag in Wikipedia's own per-member table (0 members individually tagged MAITC yet, though the assembly's aggregate reports 15) -- not something this file's authors invented, and not corrected here because doing so would require asserting individual DTC vs MAITC membership this verifier cannot source. AS and SK entity stats sums match their member rosters exactly with no discrepancy. Cross-checked the pre-existing data/raw/states-wb-as-sk.json and confirmed its entity had 'MAITC: 1' for Assam before this segment's patch (st-as-assembly notes) corrected it to 'AITC: 1' -- that correction is accurate (Assam's TMC winner predates the May 2026 WB TMC split).
